records.flowers: Pedicels to 30 mm, calyx lobes to 0.5 mm; pink/purple corolla 20–23 mm with two yellow throat lines and many small red-purple dots; source key short racemes 3–4 pairs of pedicels and internal narrow hair line below posterior sinus
records.note: Source states Texas endemic; independent county-level BONAP verification pending
records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.flowers: Pedicels 1–3 mm; calyx tube 3.5–5 mm with acute lobes; corolla 20–32 mm, deep pink to white/lavender tinged, two yellow lines and small dark-purple throat spots; key calyx lobes as long or longer than tube
records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.habit: Slender scabrous-pilose root-hemiparasitic perennial to ca. 80 cm, usually unbranched erect stems
records.leaves: Opposite/subopposite sessile elliptic-linear-lanceolate blades to 10 cm, entire to coarsely few-toothed, dark green blackening in drying, larger three-ribbed
records.flowers: Terminal nearly leafless spikes, purple/violet/lavender-pink rarely white four-unequal-lobed corolla with tube 7–15 mm and lobes 3–8 mm
records.habitat: Sandy soils, prairies, open woods, wet ground
records.note: No flowering time stated in individual 1999 treatment; leave null
records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.habit: Hemiparasitic annual from slender taproot; pubescent (genus/key)
records.leaves: Sessile/subsessile, mostly entire except lowermost; bracts entire or with small apical lobes
records.flowers: Dense terminal bracted spike with usually orange-red to red showy bract/calyx tips; corolla 20–28 mm, upper hood 6–9 mm
records.habitat: Sandy or silty open woods, prairies, disturbed sites
records.note: Flora describes rare light-yellow plants and reports natural hybridization/introgression with C. purpurea
records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.habit: Root-hemiparasitic perennial with woody root (species group/key)
records.flowers: Corollas 25–40 mm, hood 9–13 mm (C. purpurea group), bract/calyx tips yellowish orange, brownish-orange, orangish-red or red; lower lip typically 1.5–3(–4) mm (variety key)
records.habitat: Calcareous gravelly, sandy or clay soils
records.taxonomy: CRITICAL crosswalk: repository species Castilleja lindheimeri versus 1999 C. purpurea var. lindheimeri. The flora calls it weakly differentiated and reports a sharp geographic transition; do not assume current rank without verification.
records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.flowers: Variable colored floral bracts and calyx tips; corollas 25–40 mm, hood 9–13 mm; source distinguishes vars. citrina, lindheimeri, purpurea by tip color and lower corolla lip size
records.habitat: Calcareous prairie, rocky or sandy sites depending on variety
records.phenology: Mar–May in vars. lindheimeri/purpurea; Apr–May in var. citrina
records.taxonomy: Source is broad species covering three varieties; potential hybridization with C. indivisa and among varieties documented.
records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.habit: Low annual 10–15(–20) cm, unbranched to much branched
records.leaves: Opposite petiolate blades triangular-ovate in outline, 1–3 cm long, pinnately to bipinnately parted
records.flowers: Single or paired axillary flowers on pedicels 5–10 mm, pink/pale lavender tubular corollas 3–5 mm, shorter than to barely exceeding calyces; 4 didynamous stamens
records.habitat: Wet low ground and urban weedy sites
records.taxonomy: Source notes uncertain generic limits of Leucospora/Stemodia complex; modern status requires separate taxon check.
records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.habit: Twining much-branched glabrous perennial herbaceous vine; leaf petioles coiling
records.leaves: Subopposite to generally alternate, hastate to sagittate blades 15–25 mm, entire, petioles 10–30 mm
records.flowers: Solitary axillary flowers, pedicels 10–30(–47) mm, bilabiate corollas 20–25 mm, pale tube and violet/blue/purple lobes; 4 stamens and capsules ~6 mm per continuation
records.habitat: Sandy/rocky disturbed sites, Burnet and Travis region (historical flora)
records.taxonomy: Historical authors explicitly rejected segregation into Maurandella despite Kartesz treatment. Repository now uses Maurandella; source's description under Maurandya.
records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.habit: Often basal-branched glabrous procumbent to ascending wet-site perennial, stems four-angled to 40 cm
records.leaves: Opposite ovate to obovate blades 10–25 mm, serrate above middle; glandular-punctate
records.flowers: Pedicels longer than subtending leaf; outer sepals over three times width of inner; yellow corollas 6–12 mm with dark venation; genus two bractlets at pedicel base
records.habitat: Wet low ground or shallow water
records.taxonomy: Do not treat misapplied M. vandellioides usage as secure homotypic synonym.
records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.leaves: Ovate-elliptic to obovate blades sharply toothed or subentire, mid-stem usually 25–50 mm wide
records.flowers: Large white to lavender corollas with red-purple internal nectar guides; lanceolate to lance-ovate calyx lobes; genus staminode present
records.habitat: Limestone prairies, rock outcrops and sandy open woods
records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.flowers: Corollas lavender/pink/rose or red, throat white with red stripes; source key corolla 30–35 mm and sepals 8–11 mm; staminode lightly yellow-bearded on terminal half in lumped taxon
records.habitat: Calcareous soils of Edwards Plateau and southwestern north-central Texas
records.taxonomy: 1999 flora treats subsp. integrifolius and lumps P. helleri while citing possible distinctness; red-flowered P. triflorus versus lavender/pink P. helleri differentiated by staminode and corolla. No conflating subspecies/species-wide.
records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.habit: Stout biennial 0.7–2 m, densely gray felted/woolly with stellate or tree-branched hairs
records.leaves: Largest rosette blades to 50 cm, progressively smaller up stem, stem leaves sessile and decurrent
records.flowers: Terminal densely bracted spike, subsessile yellow corollas 12–30(–35) mm across; genus 5 stamens
records.fruit: Capsules densely tomentose with branched hairs, numerous seeds (genus)
records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
